paragraphs.title: The Command and the Departure for War

easy.explanation: The LORD commanded Moses to take vengeance against the Midianites.
easy.q: Against whom did the LORD command Moses to take vengeance?

easy.explanation: One thousand men were sent from every tribe.
easy.q: How many men were sent from each tribe?

easy.explanation: Moses sent Phinehas the son of Eleazar the priest with them.
easy.q: Who was sent with the men of war?

medium.explanation: One thousand men from each of the twelve tribes made twelve thousand armed men.
medium.q: How many armed men were sent from all the tribes of Israel?

medium.explanation: They went to war with the holy instruments and trumpets.
medium.q: What accompanied the men of war?

medium.explanation: The command means to prepare or equip men for war.
medium.q: In the KJV, what does “Arm some of yourselves unto the war” mean?

answers: The war was to occur before Moses was gathered to his people
challenge.explanation: The LORD said Moses would be gathered to his people after Israel took vengeance on Midian.
challenge.q: What connection does the passage make between the command and Moses’s future death?

answers: One thousand were sent from every tribe
challenge.explanation: An equal number was sent from every tribe.
challenge.q: Which detail shows that the army represented all Israel?

answers: The campaign was presented as a commanded and sacred action
The spoil had already been divided
challenge.explanation: The passage emphasizes both priestly leadership and sacred instruments.
challenge.q: What may be inferred from sending Phinehas with the holy instruments and trumpets?

paragraphs.title: The War Against Midian and the Spoils

easy.explanation: The Israelites slew all the males.
easy.q: What did Israel do to the males of Midian?

answers: Evi, Rekem, Zur, Hur, and Reba
easy.explanation: The passage names five kings of Midian: Evi, Rekem, Zur, Hur, and Reba.
easy.q: Which kings of Midian were slain?

easy.explanation: They burned the cities and their goodly castles with fire.
easy.q: What did Israel do to the cities and castles of Midian?

medium.explanation: They took the women and little ones, cattle, flocks, and goods.
medium.q: What did the children of Israel take from Midian?

answers: To the camp in the plains of Moab
medium.explanation: They brought them to the camp at the plains of Moab near Jericho.
medium.q: Where did they bring the captives, prey, and spoil?

medium.explanation: The phrase refers to the fortified places belonging to the Midianites.
medium.q: In the KJV, what are “goodly castles” in this context?

answers: The passage mentions captives, cattle, flocks, and goods
The passage mentions only the kings
The passage mentions only the castles
challenge.explanation: The text distinguishes between captives and various kinds of property.
challenge.q: Which detail shows that the spoil included both people and property?

answers: He was slain with the sword
challenge.explanation: Balaam the son of Beor was slain with the sword.
challenge.q: What happened to Balaam according to the passage?

answers: War, the slaying of enemies, taking spoil, and bringing it to the camp
Dividing spoil, then fighting and burning cities
challenge.explanation: The passage describes the campaign, the victory, the spoil, and its return to the camp.
challenge.q: What is the main order of events in this paragraph?

paragraphs.title: Purification of the Returnees and Objects

easy.explanation: Moses was wroth with the officers, captains over thousands and hundreds.
They were commanded to abide outside the camp seven days.
easy.q: How long were the returning soldiers to remain outside the camp?

easy.explanation: Those who had killed or touched the slain were to purify themselves on the third and seventh days.
easy.q: On which days were the people to purify themselves?

answers: The women had been involved in Israel’s trespass through Balaam’s counsel
medium.explanation: Moses connected them with the counsel of Balaam and the matter of Peor.
medium.q: Why did Moses command the males and certain women to be killed?

answers: It was to go through the fire and then be purified with water
It was to go through water only
medium.explanation: Objects that could abide the fire were to go through fire and the water of separation.
medium.q: What was to be done to an object that could abide the fire?

medium.explanation: The instructions concern ceremonial cleansing before reentering the camp.
medium.q: In the KJV, what does “purify” mean in these verses?

answers: The first went through fire, while the second went through water
The first was washed, while the second was burned
challenge.explanation: Eleazar distinguished between objects purified by fire and those purified by water.
challenge.q: What was the difference between objects that could abide the fire and those that could not?

answers: They had to wash their clothes on the seventh day and be clean
They had to divide the spoil
They had to send Phinehas away
challenge.explanation: After washing their clothes and becoming clean, they could come into the camp.
challenge.q: What had to happen before the returnees entered the camp?

answers: Rebuke and separation, purification of people and clothing, and cleansing of objects
Entering the camp, fighting, and burning cities
Counting the spoil, dividing it, and departing for war
challenge.explanation: The paragraph gives instructions concerning the people, clothing, and vessels before their return.
challenge.q: Which sequence best summarizes the instructions?

paragraphs.title: Division of the Spoils and Contributions

easy.explanation: The spoil was divided between those who went to battle and all the congregation.
easy.q: Between whom was the spoil divided?

easy.explanation: One soul or item of five hundred was taken from the soldiers’ half.
easy.q: What tribute was taken from the soldiers’ half?

easy.explanation: The tribute from the soldiers’ half was given to Eleazar the priest.
easy.q: To whom was the LORD’s heave offering from the soldiers’ half given?

medium.explanation: One portion of fifty was taken from the congregation’s half.
medium.q: What was the rate of the levy from the congregation’s half?

medium.explanation: It was given to the Levites, who kept the charge of the tabernacle.
medium.q: To whom was the levy from the congregation’s half given?

answers: A portion or levy taken from the spoil
medium.explanation: The tribute was a specified portion set apart from the spoil.
medium.q: In these verses, what does “tribute” mean?

answers: The levy had to be calculated separately from the soldiers’ and congregation’s shares
The cities had to be separated
The kings had to be selected
challenge.explanation: The two halves had different levy rates, so each had to be calculated separately.
challenge.q: Why was the spoil divided before the tributes were taken?

answers: Each received half, but the levy rate was different
challenge.explanation: The spoil was divided equally, but one of five hundred came from one half and one of fifty from the other.
challenge.q: What was the difference between the soldiers’ share and the congregation’s share?

answers: Keeping the charge of the tabernacle
challenge.explanation: The Levites are identified as those who kept the charge of the tabernacle of the LORD.
challenge.q: What duty of the Levites is described?

easy.explanation: The total number of sheep was six hundred seventy-five thousand.
easy.q: How many sheep were in the spoil?

easy.explanation: The passage records threescore and twelve thousand beeves, or seventy-two thousand cattle.
easy.q: How many beeves were in the spoil?

easy.explanation: The total number of such women was thirty-two thousand.
easy.q: How many women who had not known man were counted?

medium.explanation: The passage records sixty-one thousand asses.
medium.q: How many asses were in the spoil?

answers: Three hundred thirty-seven thousand five hundred
medium.explanation: The soldiers’ half contained three hundred thirty-seven thousand five hundred sheep.
medium.q: How many sheep were in the soldiers’ half?

medium.explanation: The LORD’s tribute from the sixteen thousand persons was thirty-two persons.
medium.q: How many persons were taken as the LORD’s tribute?

answers: The two halves contained equal numbers of each kind of spoil
The soldiers received twice as much
challenge.explanation: The listed numbers show that the spoil was divided into equal halves.
challenge.q: What does comparing the soldiers’ half with the congregation’s half show?

answers: It was given to the Levites
It was given to the kings of Midian
challenge.explanation: Moses gave that portion to the Levites who kept the charge of the tabernacle.
challenge.q: What was done with the levy taken from the congregation’s half?

challenge.explanation: The soldiers’ half included 337,500 sheep and 16,000 persons.
challenge.q: Which statement correctly compares the sheep and persons in the soldiers’ half?

answers: That not one man was missing
That the spoil had been lost
That the cities had not burned
easy.explanation: They reported that there lacked not one man under their charge.
easy.q: What did the army commanders report to Moses?

easy.explanation: They brought jewels of gold, chains, bracelets, rings, earrings, and tablets.
easy.q: What did the army commanders bring as an offering?

answers: Into the tabernacle of the congregation
easy.explanation: Moses and Eleazar brought the gold into the tabernacle of the congregation.

answers: The captains of thousands and hundreds
medium.explanation: The officers and captains over thousands and hundreds came to Moses with the offering.
medium.q: Who brought the offering to Moses?

answers: To make an atonement for their souls
To divide it among the soldiers
medium.explanation: They brought it to make an atonement for their souls before the LORD.
medium.q: Why did they say they brought the gold?

answers: A covering or offering for reconciliation
medium.explanation: The gold was presented as an offering of atonement before the LORD.
medium.q: In the KJV, what does “atonement” mean in this passage?

answers: Their complete survival led them to express gratitude and seek atonement
The report concerned the division of cities
challenge.explanation: After reporting that every man remained, the commanders offered gold before the LORD.
challenge.q: What is the connection between the report that no man was missing and the offering?

answers: It was given collectively by the commanders as an offering, not kept as personal spoil
It was found only in the cities
It was given to the kings of Midian
challenge.explanation: The commanders brought their gold ornaments as an offering before the LORD.
challenge.q: What was distinctive about the gold that was brought?

answers: It served as a memorial for the children of Israel before the LORD
It was used to build cities
It was immediately divided among the captives
challenge.explanation: The gold was brought into the tabernacle for a memorial before the LORD.
challenge.q: What was the significance of bringing the gold into the tabernacle?
